sections.title: The letter Er
paragraphs: The letter name is (Er) /ɛʁ/. The main sound is heard in the word (Rot) /ʁoːt/, which means red. This letter makes two sounds in German.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, pull the back of your tongue toward the throat. Let the air scrape through. Touch your throat to feel it shake. For the second sound, relax your tongue and mouth. Open your lips slightly. Make a short open vowel sound without any scrape.

sections.title: Reading the variants
paragraphs: At the start of a word or between vowels, you hear the scraping sound. You hear it in (hören) /ˈhøːʁən/. At the end of a syllable or after a long vowel, it becomes an open vowel. You hear this sound in (Uhr) /uːɐ̯/ and in (Vater) /ˈfaːtɐ/.

sections.title: Avoiding pitfalls
paragraphs: Do not curl the tip of your tongue back like in the English word red. Keep your tongue tip low behind your bottom teeth. Make the scraping sound deep in the throat. Do not make an English consonant at the end of a word like father. Relax your mouth and say a quick open vowel instead.
